sourceObjectiveEnglish: Spanish 101 final conversation: Y adds an idea, pero contrasts it, porque explains a reason, and entonces signals a result or next step.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Un cambio de planes with a patient classmate. Practice spanish 101 final conversation. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Y adds an idea, pero contrasts it, porque explains a reason, and entonces signals a result or next step. Join short accurate clauses before trying long sentences.

examples.es: Soy estudiante y vivo cerca de la escuela.
examples.en: I am a student and I live near the school.
Yesterday I studied with my friends.

cards.decisionNote: Source estudiante has no gender marker; French étudiant/étudiante does. A context-free scored face needs a qualified choice.
Spanish soy states identity; French je suis can also express condition and location, so retain the identity explanation.
Spanish está groups condition/location; French est does not preserve that source distinction by itself.
Spanish la groups feminine article, it and her; French la/l’ differs by grammatical role and elision.
Source un specifies a masculine article; French un aligns in a masculine-noun context only.
Source una specifies a feminine article; French une aligns in a feminine-noun context only.
Source en groups in/on/at; French à, dans, sur and other forms depend on the phrase.
Spanish los is masculine plural article or object; French les is gender-neutral and role-dependent.

cards.sourceSpanish: Soy estudiante y vivo cerca de la escuela.
cards.sourceEnglish: I am a student and I live near the school.
cards.decisionNote: The source student is gender-neutral; French étudiant/étudiante requires a gender or a contextual rewrite. Keep the school, not the archived workshop.

cards.sourceEnglish: Yesterday I studied with my friends.
cards.proposedFrench: Hier, j’ai étudié avec mes amis.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish completed past studied is proposed with French passé composé; confirm tense progression and saved-item identity.

cards.sourceEnglish: Today we are preparing for an exam.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish estamos preparando marks ongoing action; French present can express it, while en train de is an explicit progressive alternative.

cards.sourceSpanish: Quiero ir a la biblioteca, pero está cerrada.
cards.sourceEnglish: I want to go to the library, but it is closed.
cards.proposedFrench: Je veux aller à la bibliothèque, mais elle est fermée.
cards.decisionNote: The second clause's Spanish está refers to the library; French elle est fermée keeps that antecedent.

cards.sourceSpanish: Podemos estudiar en casa porque tenemos los libros.
cards.sourceEnglish: We can study at home because we have the books.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous pouvons étudier à la maison parce que nous avons les livres.
cards.decisionNote: Source los libros retains masculine plural; French les livres is gender-neutral but contextual noun is masculine.

cards.sourceSpanish: Mañana vamos a practicar otra vez.
cards.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow we are going to practice again.
cards.proposedFrench: Demain, nous allons nous exercer encore une fois.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish vamos a practicar is a going-to plan. French allons nous exercer uses a different lexical choice; qualify practice sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: Quiero estudiar, pero la biblioteca está cerrada.
cards.sourceEnglish: I want to study, but the library is closed.
cards.proposedFrench: Je veux étudier, mais la bibliothèque est fermée.

cards.sourceSpanish: Ana tiene un libro y dos cuadernos.
cards.sourceEnglish: Ana has a book and two notebooks.
cards.proposedFrench: Ana a un livre et deux cahiers.
cards.decisionNote: Source dos cuadernos is two notebooks, not one; French deux cahiers preserves the number.

reader.sourceSpanish: Soy estudiante y vivo cerca de la escuela.
reader.sourceEnglish: I am a student and I live near the school.
reader.decisionNote: Source student is unspecified gender. French étudiant/étudiante or a contextual rewrite needs qualified choice.

reader.sourceEnglish: Yesterday I studied with my friends.
reader.proposedFrench: Hier, j’ai étudié avec mes amis.
reader.decisionNote: Source ayer estudié is completed past; French passé composé proposal needs curriculum progression review.

reader.sourceEnglish: Today we are preparing for an exam.
reader.decisionNote: Spanish estamos preparando marks an ongoing exam-preparation action; French present or en train de needs qualification.

reader.sourceSpanish: Quiero ir a la biblioteca, pero está cerrada.
reader.sourceEnglish: I want to go to the library, but it is closed.
reader.proposedFrench: Je veux aller à la bibliothèque, mais elle est fermée.
reader.decisionNote: French elle refers to the library, retaining the source closed-library antecedent.

reader.sourceSpanish: Podemos estudiar en casa porque tenemos los libros.
reader.sourceEnglish: We can study at home because we have the books.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous pouvons étudier à la maison parce que nous avons les livres.
reader.decisionNote: Spanish los is masculine plural, whereas French les is gender-neutral; contextual les livres retains books.

reader.sourceSpanish: Mañana vamos a practicar otra vez.
reader.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow we are going to practice again.
reader.proposedFrench: Demain, nous allons nous exercer encore une fois.
reader.decisionNote: French allons nous exercer is a conditional equivalent for going to practice again.

reader.sourceSpanish: Quiero estudiar, pero la biblioteca está cerrada.
reader.sourceEnglish: I want to study, but the library is closed.
reader.proposedFrench: Je veux étudier, mais la bibliothèque est fermée.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana tiene un libro y dos cuadernos.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana has a book and two notebooks.
reader.proposedFrench: Ana a un livre et deux cahiers.

reader.sourceSpanish: Vamos al café porque está abierto.
reader.sourceEnglish: We are going to the café because it is open.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous allons au café parce qu’il est ouvert.
reader.decisionNote: Café is the same place; French il est ouvert retains the café antecedent.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis no tiene dinero, entonces Ana lo invita.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis has no money, so Ana treats him.
reader.decisionNote: Source English treats him means Ana pays for Luis after the café plan. Ana l’invite alone can mean invites him without payment; select an explicit payment wording only after qualified source/French review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Estudiamos una hora y después caminamos a casa.
reader.sourceEnglish: We study for an hour and then walk home.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous étudions pendant une heure, puis nous rentrons à pied.
reader.decisionNote: Rentrons à pied implies returning home. Qualify against source walk home and preserve one-hour sequence.

reader.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow we are going to review together.
reader.decisionNote: Repasser/revoir/réviser have different review senses; réviser ensemble is conditional for study review.

archivedRedesign.title: Mener une conversation complète en français
archivedRedesign.scene: Deux collègues organisent un atelier. Une salle devient indisponible pendant l’échange; ils clarifient les besoins, comparent les options et conviennent d’un plan provisoire.
archivedRedesign.reason: The archived workshop-room negotiation changes the source beginner library, café and home-study conversation, characters and connective objective; it cannot inherit this lesson's saved positions or recordings.

sourceDecisions: The current source is a Spanish 101 final conversation at Master stage. It teaches y, pero, porque and entonces, not the archived French workshop negotiation; qualify the capstone's beginner progression before selecting content.
Source estudiante is gender-neutral; French étudiant/étudiante needs context. Spanish soy versus está distinguishes identity and condition/location, while French suis/est alone does not.
Source la, los and en group article/object and locative senses that need contextual French faces and saved-item/dictionary mapping; French les does not preserve the masculine plural marking of los.
Reader 10 treats Luis after he has no money. Ana l’invite can be an invitation without payment; a French answer must communicate the payment/treat meaning and preserve café context.

The source combines yesterday's completed study, today's ongoing exam preparation and tomorrow's plan. Qualify French tense/aspect and the final connective result, including walking home, before six modes or audio selection.
